Article Title: Why Neeraj Chopra's CWG 2026 silver meant more with Yashvir Singh by his side in Glasgow
Article Text:
Neeraj Chopra (Image credit: Agencies)

Neeraj Chopra's medal record

'It feels great to be on the podium together'



Yashvir shines on Commonwealth Games debut

NEW DELHI: Neeraj Chopra added another medal to his glittering career at the Commonwealth Games, but the silver medal was not the only reason for his smile. The Olympic champion said sharing the podium with fellow Indian Yashvir Singh made the moment even more special.Neeraj finished second in the men's javelin throw with a season-best effort of 85.83m, while Commonwealth Games debutant Yashvir Singh clinched the bronze medal with a personal best throw of 85.41m in his final attempt. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage claimed the gold with a best throw of 89.75m.Competing in only his second event of the season, Neeraj battled difficult weather conditions to throw 85.83m in his second attempt. The effort, his season best, was enough to earn him the silver medal in his second Commonwealth Games appearance. He had won the gold medal at the 2018 Commonwealth Games in Gold Coast.The CWG 2026 silver added to an already impressive medal collection that includes Olympic gold and silver, World Championships gold and silver, two Asian Games gold medals, a Commonwealth Games gold and silver, the Diamond League title, the Asian Championships gold, the South Asian Games gold and the U20 World Championships gold.Neeraj was full of praise for Yashvir, who produced the best throw of his career under pressure, and said sharing the podium with another Indian reminded him of the Asian Games medal double."It brings back memories of the Asian Games, where Saurav and I both won medals. I'm really happy that Yashvir achieved a personal best at such a crucial moment. It feels great to be on the podium together. It's always a joy to hear the national anthem play. That said, I also achieved a season-best, and my comeback is progressing well. There are more competitions ahead, so I'm very happy," Chopra told reporters.Yashvir emerged as the surprise package of the competition. The 24-year-old produced a personal best throw of 85.41m on his sixth and final attempt to win the bronze medal on his Commonwealth Games debut.He improved his previous personal best of 83.72m and finished ahead of several established names, including Anderson Peters and Arshad Nadeem.Reflecting on his medal-winning throw, Yashvir said he kept believing he could produce something special despite a slow start."This is my first international medal, and I am overjoyed. Everyone supported me, my family, my parents, everyone... I am truly happy about this... things were going a bit sluggishly at the start. At one point, my throw was around 81.3 meters. I saw that the bronze medal mark was sitting at 82 meters. I told myself, 'I've already thrown 82 meters--my personal best--in this competition, so I can definitely go beyond that. ' Things weren't going well up to the fifth throw, so for the final attempt, I decided to just go for it and see what happens. That last throw turned out really well," Singh said.
Article Summary: Neeraj chopra won silver in the men's javelin throw at the commonwealth games. The olympic champion threw 85.83m, his season-best effort. Fellow indian yashvir singh won the bronze medal with a personal best of 85.41m. Sri lanka's rumesh tharanga pathirage claimed the gold with a best throw of 89.75m.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Seven months after her father's death, 23-year-old Tripura judoka Asmita Dey wins India's first Commonwealth Games judo gold
Article Text:
Asmita Dey (Image credit: Agencies)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Asmita Dey's historic Commonwealth Games gold medal was more than just India's first-ever top finish in judo. It was the fulfilment of a dream she once feared had ended with the death of her father seven months ago. The 23-year-old from a small village in Tripura scripted history by becoming the first Indian judoka to win a Commonwealth Games gold medal after defeating Canada's Heidi Quach in a dramatic women's 48kg final.After the win, emotions took over as Asmita remembered the man who had always believed in her."When my father passed away, I thought everything had finished because he was the one who supported me," Asmita said, struggling to hold back tears after her historic triumph.Asmita conceded an early yuko and also received a penalty, allowing Quach to take control. But the Indian judoka fought back, levelled the contest and kept her composure in the Golden Score period, where she landed the decisive yuko to seal a famous victory.After winning the gold medal, Asmita said her father always encouraged her to dream beyond the limits of their small village."I am from a very small village in Tripura. People there don't dream this big.But Papa always supported me," she said.Asmita recalled how her father stood by her."Mere papa hamesha mujhe support karte the. Beech mein mujhe injury hui thi, tab papa mere liye Delhi aaye the. Dawai, ilaaj, sab kuch unhone hi sambhala tha. Mummy-papa dono bahut support karte the, lekin mummy ko zyada samay nahi milta tha. Phir achanak 15 December ko papa ki death ho gayi. Uske baad laga ki sab kuch khatam ho gaya. Mujhe laga ki main kuch nahi kar paungi," she said."Papa jaane se pehle keh gaye the ki tum apne sapne ko aage badhana. Tum SAI Bhopal chale jao. Wahan SAI Bhopal mein mujhe bahut support mila. Thank you so much sir, kyunki main usi support ki wajah se aage badhi," Asmita said.
Article Summary: Asmita dey became the first indian judoka to win a commonwealth games gold medal. The 23-year-old defeated canada's heidi quach in a dramatic women's 48kg final. After the win, asmita remembered the man who had always believed in her.

Article Title: Injured Tejaswin Shankar scripts history; becomes first Indian to win decathlon medal in Commonwealth Games
Article Text:
India's Tejaswin Shankar competes in the men's decathlon 110m hurdles at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Scotland, Friday, July 31, 2026. (AP Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tejaswin Shankar became the first Indian to win a Commonwealth Games medal in the men's decathlon after battling a long-standing knee injury to claim bronze in Glasgow on Friday.The national record holder finished with a total of 7,976 points in the 10-event competition, which is held over two days. He competed despite dealing with chronic patellar tendinitis, also known as jumper's knee, an injury that had forced him to withdraw from the men's high jump event earlier in the Games.The 27-year-old was left emotional after having to pull out of the high jump following his opening attempt because of the injury flare-up.This was Tejaswin's second Commonwealth Games medal after winning bronze in the men's high jump at the 2022 Birmingham Games. His national record in the decathlon stands at 8,057 points.Tejaswin, who also won silver in the decathlon at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games, ended the opening day in second place after five events, behind Canada's Damian Warner.He moved into third after the ninth event, the javelin throw, and held on to that position after finishing fifth in the 1,500m, the final event of the competition.Grenada's Lindon Victor, the Paris Olympics bronze medallist, won the gold with 8,096 points, while Warner took the silver with 8,036 points."I don't know if it was adversity or not. But I do know that the competitiveness in me is alive, and in these conditions and environment, I got the kick and the competitiveness," he said, as quoted by news agency PTI."I feel good to be in that position where I want to chase something but it is not guaranteed (to get success or not). I feel I am an adrenalin junkie ... I was enjoying the challenge, when I was standing for the 1500m (the last of the 10 events).""I will try to get that feeling back, get fitter and healthier and go and try to win gold in the Asian Games."
Article Summary: Tejaswin shankar becomes first indian to win a commonwealth games medal. The 27-year-old won bronze in the men's decathlon in glasgow on friday. He competed despite dealing with chronic patellar tendinitis, also known as jumper's knee.

Article Title: Jake Dennis on taking the championship lead: “It's going to be an incredible fight with the five of us”
Article Text:
Jake Dennis at Tokyo E-Prix. (Image credit: Instagram)

Jake Dennis on becoming the new Formula E championship leader



Jake Dennis on securing another podium at the Tokyo E-Prix



Andretti driver Jake Dennis enjoyed a strong run in China this season, with three podiums in four races. After securing a podium in Shanghai, he went on to claim podium finishes on both days of the Tokyo E-Prix this weekend. While he finished second in Round 14, he claimed another podium by finishing third in Round 15. With this run of results, Dennis moved to the top of the Drivers' Standings. Just two more races remain before either Dennis, Mitch Evans or Pascal Wehrlein claims the world championship this season.Formula E dedicated a post to Dennis, which read: “There’s a new Championship leader. Jake Dennis heads to the London E-Prix on top of the Drivers’ World Championship standings.”On taking the lead from Mitch Evans in the Drivers' Standings, Dennis said, “Championship leader sounds incredible! I had this pressure back in Season 9, so I'm used to it. There's no difference there. Obviously, the gap is much closer, but you know, I'm just fully motivated, focused to get the job done, and it's going to be an incredible fight with the five of us who can probably go for it. There's no one I'd rather have backing my corner than Andretti, and let’s go and get it done in a couple of weeks.When asked about how he managed to claim a podium on Sunday, Jake Dennis said, “I think at one point I was 35 seconds back from the leader and to almost win it with no safety car or anything is pretty impressive. You know we got the call perfectly on the strategy with the tyre pressures and ultimately I just had a mega car. You know we were so quick on 300 and obviously on the 350 it was there for the taking.”Jake Dennis shared a few pictures from the podium celebrations with champagne on Instagram. He wrote: “P3. Championship leader. One round. One goal. London… let’s do this.”Reacting to his post, a fan wrote: “So deserved mate! Be cheering you on to bring it home in London!” Another called him the “Silver Surfer” for his silver merchandise for the Tokyo E-Prix.Nyck de Vries of Mahindra Racing won the Round 15 race on Sunday, with Nick Cassidy of Citroen Racing finishing second.Dennis now leads the Drivers' Standings with 146 points. Jaguar TCS Racing's Mitch Evans is just two points behind on 144, while Porsche driver Pascal Wehrlein has 141 points. Nissan’s Oliver Rowland is also in the title race with 132 points. Mahindra Racing driver Edoardo Mortara is fifth in the standings with 116 points.Also read: Tokyo E-Prix round-up: All the biggest moments from Formula E's thrilling night race
Article Summary: Andretti driver jake dennis finished on the podium on both days of the tokyo e-prix. Dennis now leads the drivers' standings with 146 points. Just two more races remain before either dennis, mitch evans or pascal wehrlein claims the world championship.

Article Title: 'One day he could captain India': Selectors explain why 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was named East Zone vice-captain
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The East Zone selectors have defended their decision to appoint 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi as vice-captain for the upcoming Duleep Trophy, describing the move as part of a long-term leadership plan rather than an indication of the team's pecking order.While Ishan Kishan 's appointment as captain was widely expected, the decision to hand the vice-captaincy to Sooryavanshi drew attention, especially with experienced campaigners such as Abhimanyu Easwaran Mohammed Shami and Mukesh Kumar also part of the squad.Sooryavanshi has featured in only eight first-class matches for Bihar, while Easwaran has played 113 first-class games and previously captained Bengal, India A and other representative sides.Explaining the reasoning behind the decision, Manish Vardhan, Jharkhand's representative on the East Zone selection committee, said the move was aimed at helping the youngster understand leadership from close quarters."We are not thinking about the present alone," Vardhan told Cricinfo. "A vice-captain gets to observe the captain closely and understand how a team is run. We wanted Vaibhav to be more involved with the group because we think it will help him as he develops."He's an extremely talented cricketer and is maturing steadily. Giving him this responsibility is another part of that process."Vardhan also clarified that Sooryavanshi's appointment does not automatically make him the stand-in captain if Kishan is unavailable.Although the selectors have not discussed that possibility, he suggested that an experienced player would likely take charge while Sooryavanshi continued as vice-captain.According to Vardhan, the committee's thinking behind appointing Kishan as captain was also based on long-term planning, with both Kishan and Sooryavanshi viewed as players capable of remaining in India's setup for many years."The vice-captain's role isn't about status," Vardhan said. "It's about what a young player can learn while working alongside the captain."Former Odisha cricketer and current selector-coach Pravanjan Mullick echoed those views, pointing out that Sooryavanshi has already served as Bihar's vice-captain in first-class cricket."Ishan is the captain and, as wicketkeeper, he is involved in every phase of the game," Mullick told Cricinfo. "This gives Vaibhav an opportunity to understand leadership without putting the responsibility of captaining the side on him. We want him to grow, maybe one day he could even captain India. That's the thought behind giving him the vice-captaincy."Cricinfo also reported that Easwaran was intentionally not considered for the vice-captain's role. The selection committee reportedly felt it would not be appropriate for the vastly experienced batter to serve as deputy to the comparatively inexperienced Kishan.
Article Summary: The east zone selectors have defended their decision to appoint 15-year-old vaibhav sooryavanshi as vice-captain for the upcoming duleep trophy. Manish vardhan, jharkhand's representative on the east zone selection committee, said the move was aimed at helping the youngster understand leadership from close quarters.

Article Title: Fact Check: Is the viral photo of Jayden Daniels' mother piggybacking on him real or AI-generated?
Article Text:
Image - X

Viral Jayden Daniels photo with his mother: What we know about the image

This isn't the first time Regina Jackson's role has sparked debate

A photo of Jayden Daniels giving his mom a piggyback ride after practice is going viral, but there's a catch: the image is not real. Beyond the online uproar it's caused, the picture appears to be AI-generated, reopening a debate that's followed the Commanders quarterback for over a year: is Regina Jackson a devoted support system, or is she a little too close for comfort?The image, Daniels in pads with Jackson hopping on his back, started making rounds on X after an account called it "straight up weird," racking up over a million views in a day. But almost as fast as it spread, questions arose about whether the photo was actually authentic.Commanders quarterbacks reportedly don't wear the yellow jersey shown in the image during current practices, and the image carries some of the telltale inconsistencies associated with AI-generated content.That uncertainty didn't stop the replies from turning into a full-blown debate. Some fans pushed back hard on the dynamic itself, with one writing that things are "starting to get a little strange" and pointing to it as part of a pattern rather than a one-off. Another user went further, questioning whether it's healthy for the two to be so entangled, and predicted it would make dating difficult for Daniels down the line.But plenty of others jumped in to defend the moment, real or not, as exactly what it appeared to be: a mom being affectionate with her son. Several replies pushed back on people reading too much into it, with one pointing out that not everyone expresses love and closeness the same way, and that a wholesome gesture doesn't deserve to be picked apart.The split reaction is arguably what made the picture travel so quickly, real or fabricated. A single image, authentic or not, became another social media Rorschach test, with wildly different interpretations depending on who was looking at it.Regina Jackson's presence in her son's career is far from casual; she's Daniels' NFLPA-certified agent, meaning she negotiates directly with the team and has formal standing in his business affairs, not just a supportive parent showing up to camp. That level of involvement has made her a recurring lightning rod. Past viral moments involving the two of them have already sparked "helicopter mom" narratives, with some fans framing her closeness as overprotective.In contrast, others call it a genuinely close family bond that's been unfairly scrutinized simply because it plays out in public. This latest photo, whatever its origins, looks less like a new controversy and more like the same fault line resurfacing; Commanders fans, it seems, still haven't made up their minds about where support ends, and something else begins.For Daniels, the attention comes at a time when virtually everything surrounding his life is magnified because of his status as one of the NFL's most recognizable young quarterbacks. It also fits a broader pattern: this isn't the first fake or manipulated image tied to Daniels to spread widely before anyone stopped to check if it was real.And that may be the biggest takeaway from the latest uproar. Whether or not the photo is genuine, it's given social media another image to interpret, and judging by the reaction, the conversation around Daniels and his mom isn't disappearing anytime soon.
Article Summary: A photo of jayden daniels giving his mom a piggyback ride after practice is going viral. But there's a catch: the image is not real. The picture appears to be ai-generated, reopening a debate that's followed the commanders quarterback for over a year.

Article Title: Why Tom Brady still “hates” the 49ers despite becoming the GOAT
Article Text:
Why Tom Brady still “hates” the 49ers 25 years after they passed on him six times

The grudge Tom Brady refuses to retire: why he still "hates" the 49ers

Twenty-five years, seven rings, and he still isn't over it

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tom Brady has seven Super Bowl rings, the most passing yards in NFL history, and absolutely nothing left to prove. And yet, 25 years later, there's still one wound that hasn't closed: the San Francisco 49ers, his hometown team, the team he grew up loving, passed on him six separate times in the 2000 NFL Draft. He has never let it go. He's not sure he ever will.Before he was the GOAT, Brady was just a Bay Area kid who idolized Joe Montana and grew up watching the 49ers dominate football in the 1980s and 90s. He was there, in some form, for the glory years, four Super Bowls, Bill Walsh's West Coast offense, Montana finding Dwight Clark for "The Catch." The 49ers weren't just a team to Brady. They were the standard.So when San Mateo's own local kid, a promising quarterback out of Michigan, entered the 2000 draft, it seemed almost written that San Francisco would call his name. They didn't. Not once, not twice, six times the 49ers took other players before finally, in the third round, settling on a different quarterback altogether: Hofstra's Giovanni Carmazzi. Brady would sit through the rest of that draft, watching team after team pass on him too, until New England scooped him up dead last in the sixth round, pick 199. The Patriots, for the record, had also passed on him five times before that, "just one less than everybody else," as Brady likes to point out.What happened next barely needs repeating: Brady became the most decorated quarterback in NFL history, while Carmazzi never played a single regular-season snap for San Francisco before retiring and, fittingly, becoming a goat farmer.It's a real-life football fable, and Brady has never resisted the urge to tell it. Every time he faced the 49ers over his 23-year career, he says, some part of him wanted to remind the men who'd been in that draft room exactly what they'd given up. "You chose a goat farmer over me," he's said, "and I never forgot that."He's repeated versions of the story for years on podcasts, in broadcast booths, in interviews timed to games against San Francisco, and each retelling carries the same mix of humor and genuine sting. He's admitted the 49ers even circled back years later, first reportedly considering him over Jimmy Garoppolo in 2020, then again in 2023 when Kyle Shanahan pursued him amid uncertainty over Brock Purdy's health. Both times, Brady said no. Whatever the reasons, it's hard not to read those refusals as their own quiet punctuation on the story Brady, for all his talk of love for the franchise, was never going back.Steve Mariucci, the 49ers' head coach at the time of the snub, has taken the ribbing in stride, noting that literally every team passed on Brady multiple times that year, and that he still loves the guy. Brady, for his part, seems to genuinely hold two things at once: real affection for the uniform he grew up watching, and real resentment toward the organization that decided, six separate times, that he wasn't good enough.He still watches their games. He still, by his own admission, can't bring himself to root for them.Twenty-five years and seven championships later, it's clear the chip on Brady's shoulder never really came off; he just found somewhere else to carry it.
Article Summary: The san francisco 49ers passed on tom brady six separate times in the 2000 nfl draft. Brady has never let it go, and he's not sure he ever will. He still watches their games, but can't bring himself to root for them.

NEW DELHI: With more than a year left for the 2027 ODI World Cup, former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin has shared the players he believes should be in the squad for the tournament.Speaking on ESPNcricinfo's YouTube channel, Ashwin divided the players into three categories - 'Yes', 'Maybe' and 'No' - while naming the cricketers he feels should be considered for the World Cup, which will be co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia from October 4 to November 21, 2027.One of Ashwin's biggest talking points was the inclusion of veteran pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar , while players such as Rishabh Pant , Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson did not make his preferred squad.: Shubman Gill , Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer, KL Rahul, Ishan Kishan, Hardik Pandya , Axar Patel, Kuldeep Yadav, Jasprit Bumrah, Mohammed Siraj, Harshit Rana, Bhuvneshwar Kumar.: Yashasvi Jaiswal, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Varun Chakravarthy, Ravindra Jadeja, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Mohammed Shami, Arshdeep Singh, Prasidh Krishna.: Rishabh Pant, Washington Sundar, Sanju Samson, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Abhishek Sharma, Ravi Bishnoi, Shivam Dube, Prince Yadav, Gurnoor Brar.Ashwin believes Bhuvneshwar can still play an important role in South African conditions and said he should be given regular game time before the World Cup."Bhuvneshwar Kumar is a yes. I would communicate to him. Get him to play all the tournaments, first-class, Vijay Hazare, everything, and get him primed going to South Africa.I think we will need him there."Bhuvneshwar impressed in IPL 2026, playing a key role in Royal Challengers Bengaluru's second straight title. He signed off the tournament's second-highest wicket-taker with 28 wickets in 16 matches, averaging 17.89 with an economy rate of 7.95.The experienced seamer has also enjoyed a successful ODI career, taking 141 wickets in 121 matches at an average of 35.11, with best figures of 5/42. Across all international formats, he has claimed 294 wickets in 229 matches.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge

Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit







El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. That is what stayed with people.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Pablo Picasso: "When I was as old as these children, I could draw like Raphael, but it took me a lifetime to learn to…" - a profound lesson on creativity, simplicity and rediscover
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Pablo Picasso (Image: Wikipedia)

Quote of the day by Pablo Picasso

"When I was as old as these children, I could draw like Raphael, but it took me a lifetime to learn to draw like them"

What the quote actually means

Where this quote actually comes from

Why real mastery is more than technical skill

Why children create so freely in the first place

Why fear so often gets in the way of real creativity

Why simplicity is often the harder, more impressive achievement

Why curiosity should never really disappear with age

A note on Picasso's own artistic journey

Other memorable quotes by Pablo Picasso

"Everything you can imagine is real."

"Every child is an artist. The problem is how to remain an artist once we grow up."

"I paint objects as I think them, not as I see them."

"Learn the rules like a pro, so you can break them like an artist."

Why this quote is relevant

Quote of the day by Pablo Picasso: "When I was as old as these children, I could draw like Raphael, but it took me a lifetime to learn to…" - a profound lesson on creativity, simplicity and rediscovering the fearless artist withinChildren draw without hesitation, painting exactly what they imagine rather than what anyone expects of them. Pablo Picasso pointed at that exact quality with real admiration. "When I was as old as these children, I could draw like Raphael," he said, "but it took me a lifetime to learn to draw like them." A popular shortened version of this line, "it took me my whole life to learn to draw like a child," circulates far more widely, but it leaves out the actual comparison that gives the thought its real bite, the specific gap between a technique that took years to master and a freedom that came naturally to children without any training at all.Picasso is not claiming children's drawings are technically superior to a trained artist's work. He is admiring what sits behind them, working entirely without fear, experimenting freely, driven by imagination rather than any concern for getting things exactly right. As artists become more skilled, they tend to become far more aware of rules, expectations and the possibility of criticism. Picasso believed genuine creativity meant combining real technical mastery with that same fearless imagination children have naturally, before anyone has taught them to be self-conscious about it.The fuller version of this line, with the direct comparison to Raphael, is documented in Ingo F. Walther's book Picasso, part of the Basic Art series. The most widely repeated popular paraphrase reads, "It took me four years to paint like Raphael, but a lifetime to paint like a child," which trims the wording slightly differently but keeps the same essential comparison. The much shorter version usually quoted today, "it took me my whole life to learn to draw like a child," drops the Raphael reference entirely, which is really the detail that makes the original observation land properly, since it directly measures technical mastery against something children manage without ever being taught it at all.Most people assume expertise simply means becoming more precise over time. Picasso's own career complicates that idea directly. He had mastered classical, realistic drawing while still a teenager, essentially able to draw like Raphael long before he was an adult. Yet after reaching that level of technical ability, he spent decades deliberately simplifying his work and pushing into entirely new forms of expression. His own path shows that mastery was never only about knowing more. It was just as much about expressing an idea with real honesty and clarity, however simple the final result actually looked.Children rarely worry about making a mistake before they even start. They paint purple trees and flying elephants without a second thought, because they have not yet learned to fear being wrong about anything. That openness is exactly what allows genuine experimentation, and plenty of real breakthroughs in science, business and art begin with someone willing to ask a question that sounds a little unusual or unrealistic at first.As people get older, they tend to become far more preoccupied with how something will be judged. Will people approve of it. Will the idea simply fail. Will it make me look foolish. These worries discourage the kind of experimentation Picasso is describing, and his own quote is really an invitation to recover the confidence to explore an idea without letting perfectionism quietly block the way first.Complexity tends to impress people on the surface. Genuine simplicity usually requires a much deeper understanding underneath it. Whether in painting, writing or plain communication, expressing something genuinely meaningful in a clear, accessible way turns out to be remarkably difficult in practice. Picasso seemed to believe that simplicity earned through real experience represented a higher form of creativity than complexity created purely for its own sake.Children ask endless questions, why, how, what if, without any embarrassment about not already knowing the answer. Holding onto that same curiosity through adulthood tends to encourage genuine lifelong learning. People who keep exploring, questioning and experimenting well into their careers tend to stay more innovative than people who quietly stop asking those questions once they feel sufficiently expert.Picasso showed extraordinary technical skill from a genuinely young age, producing highly realistic paintings while still a teenager. Later, he became a pioneer of Cubism, continually reinventing his own artistic style across an unusually long career. His quote reflects the belief that while technique can be taught fairly directly, holding onto imagination, spontaneity and real originality is closer to a lifelong pursuit than a skill someone simply finishes learning.In a world that often rewards efficiency, correctness and simply fitting in, Picasso's line is a reminder of what imagination is actually worth, the courage to create freely, the willingness to get things wrong along the way, and the ability to see real possibility where other people only see limitations. None of that belongs exclusively to children. It stays available to anyone still willing to hold onto it.
Article Summary: Quote of the day by pablo picasso: "when i was as old as these children, i could draw like raphael, but it took me a lifetime to learn to draw like them" a profound lesson on creativity, simplicity and rediscovering the fearless artist within.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Taylor Swift: ‘My response to anything that happens, good or bad, is to keep making things,’ and how creativity can outlast every setback
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Taylor Swift

“My response to anything that happens, good or bad, is to keep making things.” —

Taylor Swift

The meaning behind the quote

All Too Well

Clean

Anti-Hero

You're On Your Own, Kid

Creativity as a way of moving forward

Harry Potter

Across nearly two decades, Taylor Swift has written songs inspired by heartbreak, friendship, criticism, public scrutiny and personal milestones, transforming private experiences into albums that have resonated with millions. Whether celebrating success or navigating disappointment, one pattern has remained unchanged: she keeps creating.That mindset is captured in one of her most memorable reflections. Rather than treating creativity as something that appears only during moments of inspiration, Taylor Swift presents it as a way of responding to life itself. The quote suggests that making something— a song, a painting, a story, a photograph or even a simple journal entry— can become an act of resilience, regardless of what life brings.The quote stands out because it makes no distinction between success and failure. Many people feel inspired to create when life is going well or turn to art only during periods of struggle. Taylor Swift’s philosophy embraces both. Joy becomes something worth celebrating, while setbacks become experiences that can be understood, processed and transformed into something new.In this sense, creativity is less about talent than about habit.It becomes a way of meeting the world instead of merely reacting to it. Every experience, pleasant or painful, offers material for reflection and expression.Psychologists have long recognised the value of creative expression in helping people make sense of difficult emotions. Research has shown that writing, music, painting and other forms of creativity can help people process stressful experiences, organise their thoughts and improve emotional well-being. The goal is not to erase hardship but to give it shape, making it easier to understand and move forward.Taylor Swift's own career reflects that approach. Songs such asanddraw from deeply personal experiences while speaking to universal emotions. Over the years, her music has documented different stages of life, showing that even difficult chapters can become part of a larger creative journey.The quote also shifts attention away from outcomes. It does not say to keep succeeding, winning or proving yourself. It simply says to keep making things. That subtle difference matters because creative work is one of the few pursuits where the act itself can be rewarding, regardless of recognition or commercial success.History is filled with artists, writers and inventors whose greatest work emerged after periods of uncertainty, rejection or personal loss. J.K. Rowling began writingwhile facing financial hardship. Vincent van Gogh continued painting despite receiving little recognition during his lifetime. Frida Kahlo transformed chronic pain into some of the twentieth century's most celebrated artworks. Their circumstances differed, but they shared a common instinct: to continue creating.The same principle extends far beyond artists. A teacher designing better lessons after a difficult semester, an entrepreneur developing a new idea after a failed business, or a home cook experimenting with new recipes after moving to a different city are all responding to change by making something new. Creativity is not confined to studios or concert halls. It is present wherever people choose to build instead of retreat.Taylor’s quote also reflects an important truth about resilience. Recovery is rarely passive. People move forward by taking action, however small. Creating something— a page of writing, a sketch, a melody or a new idea— can restore a sense of purpose when circumstances feel uncertain.In a world that often measures achievement through awards, numbers and public approval, the quote offers a quieter perspective. The value of creativity does not lie only in what it produces but in what it allows us to become. Every finished piece is evidence that we chose to continue despite whatever came before it.That may be why Taylor Swift’s words resonate with so many people. Life will continue to bring moments of celebration and disappointment in equal measure. We cannot control every event, but we can choose our response. For Taylor Swift, that response is simple: keep making things. In doing so, creativity becomes more than a skill or a profession and becomes a way of carrying hope, curiosity and resilience through every chapter of life.
Article Summary: Quote of the day by taylor swift: ‘my response to anything that happens, good or bad, is to keep making things’ creativity is not confined to studios or concert halls. It is present wherever people choose to build instead of retreat. People move forward by taking action, however small.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Tiger Woods: "Talent is something you are born with, and a skill is something you…" - a lesson on why practice matters more than natural ability
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Tiger Woods (Getty Images)

Quote of the day by Tiger Woods

The deeper meaning of Tiger Wood’s quote

Why Woods himself is the perfect person to say this

Why skill keeps growing while talent stays roughly where it started

Why consistent practice tends to beat raw potential

Why repeating the basics is what actually builds mastery

Why mistakes end up teaching more than easy wins do

Why discipline tends to matter more than motivation

Other famous quotes by Tiger Woods



"No matter how good you get you can always get better, and that's the exciting part."

"Achievements on the golf course are not what matters, decency and honesty are what matter."

"Other golfers may outplay me from time to time, but they'll never outwork me."

"We all make decisions. But in the end, our decisions make us."

Why this quote is relevant

Watching a champion perform can make success look effortless, as though it were simply handed to a lucky few at birth. Tiger Woods pushed back on that idea directly. "Talent is something you are born with, and a skill is something you develop," he said. "99% of what you need to succeed in golf are skills." Talent might give someone a starting point. What actually determines how far they get is what they choose to practise and refine every single day after that, a lesson that Woods himself spent decades proving through his own extraordinarily disciplined career. What gives this quote unusual weight is that Woods didn't just say it once and move on. He proved it repeatedly, rebuilding his swing and his body after injury after injury, when relying purely on natural gift would have quietly ended his career years earlier."Talent is something you are born with, and a skill is something you develop. 99% of what you need to succeed in golf are skills"Woods draws a clear line between two very different things. Talent is natural ability, something someone may already have from a young age. Skill is something earned, built up through repetition, discipline, learning from mistakes and steady, continuous improvement, none of which arrives automatically no matter how talented someone started out.Saying that 99% of golfing success comes from skill is Woods arguing that raw natural ability, on its own, is almost never enough. Even the most naturally gifted players still need thousands of hours refining the basics and correcting weaknesses. The quote shifts attention away from what someone was simply born with and toward what they can actually control through effort.Woods has been blunt about his own background in the past. "People don't understand that when I grew up, I was never the most talented," he said. "I was never the biggest. I was never the fastest. I certainly was never the strongest. The only thing I had was my work ethic, and that's been what has gotten me this far." That is not a modest exaggeration. It is exactly the same claim the main quote is making, just told from the inside.Across a career spanning decades, Woods has won 15 major championships and 82 PGA Tour events, a total that ties him for the most wins in PGA Tour history. His success was never built on natural ability alone. It came from relentless practice, physical conditioning, mental preparation and constant technical adjustment, and after multiple serious injuries and surgeries, he rebuilt his game more than once through exactly the same patience and hard work his quote describes, refusing to simply rely on the natural gifts everyone assumed had carried him this far already.Natural talent might give someone a real head start early on, but skill keeps developing for as long as someone keeps working on it. A gifted musician still practises scales every day. An experienced surgeon still keeps learning new techniques years into their career. Nearly every profession rewards people who keep improving long after their natural strengths have already become obvious to everyone. Skill, unlike raw talent, is cumulative. Every hour spent genuinely learning adds a little more competence, confidence and consistency to what came before it.Potential only actually means something once it gets developed. Plenty of people with real natural gifts never fully use them because they lean too heavily on simply being gifted. Others, starting from a far more ordinary place, end up surpassing them purely through years of consistent practice. Sport shows this pattern constantly. Athletes with disciplined training habits generally outperform equally talented rivals who never prepared properly. The same pattern shows up in business, education, music and almost everywhere else too.Mastery rarely arrives through one dramatic breakthrough. It usually comes from repeating simple actions until they become second nature. Professional golfers spend enormous amounts of time on short putts, bunker shots and basic swing mechanics, and those small, repeated improvements are ultimately what separate elite performers from everyone else. The same is true elsewhere. Pilots rehearse emergency procedures long before they might ever need one. Excellence usually comes from repetition rather than a sudden flash of inspiration.Developing any real skill involves failing along the way, missed shots, disappointing rounds, rejected ideas. All of that failure carries useful information for anyone actually paying attention to it. Woods has spoken about analysing his own poor rounds directly rather than ignoring them, treating every mistake as part of the learning process rather than something to brush past.Motivation rises and falls depending on the day. Discipline is what keeps someone practising even once the initial enthusiasm has faded. People who wait to feel inspired before doing the work tend to make patchy, inconsistent progress. People who simply build a routine keep improving steadily regardless of how motivated they happen to feel on any given day.Modern culture tends to celebrate sudden success while skipping past the years of preparation that actually produced it. Woods' quote is a useful reminder that lasting achievement is usually built through steady, consistent effort rather than natural talent on its own. Talent might open the very first door. Skill is what actually decides how far someone gets to go after that, whatever field they happen to be working in.
Article Summary: Tiger woods' quote of the day: "99% of what you need to succeed in golf are skills" woods argues that raw natural ability, on its own, is almost never enough. Even the most naturally gifted players still need thousands of hours refining the basics. Athletes with disciplined training habits generally outperform equally talented rivals who never prepared properly.

The 7th PNB MetLife Junior Badminton Championship shattered records with over 8,200 young talent nationwide, earning global recognition and fostering a culture of resilience and determination in aspiring badminton starsIn a spectacular display of badminton prowess and youthful enthusiasm, the 7th edition of the PNB MetLife Junior Badminton Championship (JBC) etched its name in the annals of sporting history. Celebrating a staggering participation of 8257 young champions from across India, the championship not only broke its own record set in 2022 but also clinched the title of the ‘Most kids participating in a Badminton Championship in multiple cities’ as recognised by the World Record Certification Agency (WRCA).The grand finale unfolded at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi, where the air was thick with competition, camaraderie, and the unmistakable passion for badminton. The event, graced by chief guests Chirag Shetty and Satwik Rankireddy, Asian Games Gold Medalists and JBC 2023 mentors, was a true celebration of the sport’s rising stars.The 10-city extravaganza, spanning the length and breadth of the country, showcased the unwavering commitment of PNB MetLife in nurturing young talents in the badminton arena.
